That's not a BIP 101 block, that's an XT block.

Technically there is no such thing as an XT block...but most people understand that we're talking about the same thing when we say XT or BIP101...Also we don't really know if the block was mined by XT or Bitcoin Core Big Blocks, so we say BIP101.

XT is not the same thing as BIP101. XT implements BIP101, among other things.

There's no such thing as a BIP101 block. BIP101 got rejected, therefor it's still a proposal. An implementation of it isn't bitcoin anymore. I think most people agree that any version that follows the XT implementation is called "XT". Just like any version of core is still called bitcoin because they follow the rules of the reference client. Just like there are many BitTorrent clients, but once you have a client that doesn't follow the rules of the network, it's not BitTorrent anymore. It doesn't matter if the new rules where proposed in a BEP or not.

We also don't really know if a block was mined by notbitcoinxt, so if you're going that route all you can say is: a block mined by someone who advertises to follow XT rules.

edit: I realize it's a thin line to walk, but think of it this way: if BIP101 gets implemented in core, maybe with some adjustments like a different date and/or an actual supermajority instead of 75%, how are you going to call those blocks?

The blocks are marked the same. XT implements BIP 101. There is actually no ability to tell the difference between an "XT block" and a "BIP 101" block because they are marked identically. So software that is not XT but which still implements BIP 101 will mark the blocks identically.
Like I said, notbitcoinxt doesn't implement BIP 101, yet it also marks the blocks identically.
